claims.statement: A route's two travel directions are two independent `directions` rows — the admin-plotted base carries `direction_kind: "base"` and the server-derived return carries `direction_kind: "return"` — and each row owns its own `base_polyline` value and its own `stops` rows, so the return is derived once at save time and is neither a render-time reversal of one shared geometry nor a view (ADR-0008, ADR-0011).
`buildDerivedReturn` reverses the base polyline into a new coordinate array, builds new stop objects with new `location` objects and `stop_order` renumbered from 1, and never mutates the base input.

The derived return's label is always `To <first base stop name>`, computed from the unrotated base stop list, while the base label is supplied by the client as `To <last stop name>`, so the pair's labels mirror each other on an open path.

When the base has at least two stops and its last polyline coordinate lies within `ENDPOINT_TOLERANCE_METERS` (100 m) of the first stop, `buildDerivedReturn` treats the base as a closed ring and rotates the reversed stop list so the base's first stop also leads the return (stops `[A, B, C]` on a ring derive to `[A, C, B]` over `[A, C, B, A]`); on an open path the list is simply reversed.
Stop sequence comes from array position, not from client-sent `stop_order`: `normalizeStopOrder` renumbers the base's stops 1..n, and the derivation renumbers the return's stops the same way.

`persistPlottedPair` is the only code that writes both members of a pair, and it does so in a single `db.transaction`: base row, base stop rows, base terminals, derived return row, return stop rows and return terminals commit together or not at all.

In create mode the pair write counts the route's active directions inside the transaction and throws `conflict` — HTTP 409 with code `CONFLICT` — when two or more already exist, before inserting the base row.

The exactly-two-active-directions rule is a transaction-scoped `SELECT` rather than a schema constraint: `directions` carries only non-unique indexes, there is no unique constraint on `(route_id, direction_kind)`, and the guard takes no row lock, so concurrent create requests can both pass it and the admin depends on the save-time 409 plus its conflict banner and Load latest recovery.

`direction_kind` exists because both members of a pair are inserted in one transaction and therefore share the same `now()`-based `created_at`, so client-facing queries order directions by `direction_kind ASC, created_at ASC, direction_id ASC` and the enum's declaration order — `base` before `return` — puts the base first without a `CASE` expression.

The `direction_kind` marker is server-internal and never appears in an API payload — `toDirectionPayload`, `DirectionSummaryEntity` and the admin's `DirectionEntity` all omit it — so a client that needs the base relies on the server's ordering or tracks the `direction_id` it saved.

`GET /api/admin/routes/:routeId/directions` has no `ORDER BY` and returns stop-less summaries in unspecified row order, unlike the route detail and overview readers which order by kind, so its first element cannot be treated as the base.

The kind-first ordering identifies a direction's role, not the live pair: neither route detail nor overview filters `is_active`, `DELETE /api/admin/directions/:directionId` is a soft delete that leaves the row in place, and the admin seeds its editor and draft key from `directions[0]`, so a deactivated older base row can still be selected as the base.

Replace mode (`PUT /api/admin/directions/:directionId` carrying both `stops` and `base_polyline`) overwrites the target as the `base` member and re-derives or creates its active sibling as the `return` member, which keeps the pair mutual reverses while silently discarding return-side edits made since the last save, and it takes no two-active-directions count.
The sibling that replace mode re-derives is selected with `is_active = true` and `LIMIT 1` and no `ORDER BY`, so the choice is arbitrary whenever a route has more than one active sibling.

The pair write replaces stop rows wholesale — `DELETE` followed by re-insert with fresh `stop_id`s — and then points each direction's `origin_stop_id` / `destination_stop_id` at its own first and last inserted stop, so every direction's terminals resolve inside its own ordered stop list, which is the property `referenceCheck` asserts and the export integration test verifies.

Per-stop attributes on a plotted save come from the request payload rather than from the rows being replaced: the insert applies `is_guaranteed_service ?? true` and `landmark_hint` / `notes` `?? null`, never sets `ar_marker_enabled` or `is_active` (column defaults apply), and the admin's `savePlot` maps only `name`, `type` and `location`.

A plotted save passes five gates — parent exists (404), `stops` present with at least two entries (422, with `stops: []` rejected rather than treated as the legacy shape), path endpoints within 100 m of the first and last stop with a loop allowed (422 naming `start_mismatch`/`end_mismatch` and the distance), `base_polyline` required alongside `stops` in replace mode (422), and the create-mode two-active-directions count (409) — and the first four run in the handler before any transaction opens.

Any throw inside the pair transaction rolls the whole write back: a 409 leaves no base row behind, and an unexpected failure surfaces as 500 INTERNAL through the Fastify error handler with no partial state.

A `POST /api/admin/routes/:routeId/directions` without `stops` takes the legacy single-direction path: a plain insert with no transaction and no derivation, `direction_kind` defaulting to `base` and `is_active` to `true`, a response carrying `stops: []` and no `return_direction` key, and `return_polyline: null` in the overview payload.

`PUT /api/admin/directions/:directionId` without `stops` patches one row only (`label`, `base_polyline`, terminals, `is_active`) and its polyline-only form never runs the endpoint gate, because that gate is conditional on the request carrying `stops`; no admin client function calls this path today, since the workspace saves through `saveDirection` or `replaceDirection`.
`direction_count` in the route list counts every direction row of a route, including soft-deleted ones, because the grouping aggregate has no `WHERE` clause.

The pair write neither deletes nor re-validates the detours and restrictions attached to the directions it rewrites, and `assertRestrictionIndexRange` runs only in the restrictions API, so a replaced or re-derived polyline can leave a restriction's `from_coord_index` / `to_coord_index` range or a detour's entry/exit anchors stale.

Both pair responses re-read the persisted rows with `loadDirectionFull` after the commit, return the flat base payload plus an additive `return_direction` key, and the admin patches its react-query caches from that response — replacing the cached `directions` array with `[base, return]` — without a refetch.

The derivation and pair-save rules are pinned by `apps/server/tests/unit/derive.test.ts` (reversal without mutation, the return label, renumbering, closed-loop rotation, the endpoint rule, `normalizeStopOrder`) and `apps/server/tests/integration/plotting-save.test.ts` (atomic pair create with the return's own terminal ids, the 422 gates persisting nothing, loop acceptance, the third-direction 409, replace-mode re-derivation, the legacy no-stops create, base-first detail ordering, overview base/return polylines).
